meta.name: Little Two
meta.blurb: A three-player climbing card game over up to 3 deals: shed your 9 cards with singles, pairs, triples or runs; the lowest total penalty wins.

rules:
Little Two is a climbing card game for 3 players over at most {max_deals} deals and at most {max_orbits} orbits.

CARDS. There are {deck_size} cards, numbered 1 to {deck_size}. A card c has rank = floor((c+2)/3), from 1 to {ranks}, and suit = c - 3*(rank-1), from 1 to {suits}. Rank 1 is lowest and rank {ranks} (cards {top_rank_card_low} to {top_rank_card_high}) is highest and plays the role of the 2. Within a rank a higher suit is a higher card, so a higher card number is always a higher card. Card 13 is rank 5 suit 1, card 14 is rank 5 suit 2, card 16 is rank 6 suit 1.

PLAYS. A play is {min_play_cards} to {max_play_cards} cards from your own hand, written as their numbers in ascending order separated by single spaces (for example '13 14'). Single: 1 card. Pair: 2 cards of the same rank ('13 14' is a pair; '14 16' is not). Triple: 3 cards of the same rank. Run: {run_length} cards whose ranks are three consecutive numbers, in any suits; ranks do not wrap around. Any other set of cards is not a play. The value of a play is its highest card number.

DEALS. A deal starts at the beginning of an orbit when no deal is active and fewer than {max_deals} deals have started. All {deck_size} cards are shuffled, each player gets {hand_size} private cards and {aside_size} cards are set aside unseen. Seat 1 leads deal 1, seat 2 leads deal 2, seat 3 leads deal 3. The pile starts empty.

TURNS. Each orbit, seats take turns in order 1, 2, 3. A seat skips its turn if no deal is active, or if it is the orbit in which the deal started and its seat number is lower than the leader's. If the last play on the pile is your own (the other two have passed since, or the deal has just started), the pile is cleared and you lead.
- Pile empty (you lead): you may play any single, pair, triple or run from your hand. You may not pass.
- Pile is a single: pass, play a higher single, or play any triple (a bomb).
- Pile is a pair: pass, play a pair with a higher value, or play any triple (a bomb).
- Pile is a triple: pass, or play a triple with a higher value.
- Pile is a run: pass, or play a run with a higher value.
You are only offered legal choices. Everyone sees every play and pass. If you pass, nothing changes except that your last action shows 'pass'; you may play again when your turn comes round. If you play, the cards leave your hand, your card count drops, and your play becomes the pile: 1 card is a single, 2 a pair, 3 of one rank a triple, 3 consecutive ranks a run. A triple that bombs a single or pair makes the pile a triple, so only a higher triple can follow it.

WINNING A DEAL. When you play your last card you win the deal: your deals won rises by 1 and the deal ends at once; the rest of that orbit's turns are skipped. Every other player with n cards left adds n penalty points, or {double_penalty_factor} times n if n is {double_penalty_threshold} or more, plus {top_card_penalty} for each card numbered {top_rank_card_low} to {top_rank_card_high} still in hand (7 cards including card 30 adds 15).

END. The game ends when deal {max_deals} has ended, or when orbit {max_orbits} is complete. If orbit {max_orbits} ends during a deal, every player is penalised by the same formula for the cards they hold. Deals that never started are not played. The lowest total penalty wins; among players tied for lowest, the one with the most deals won wins; players still tied share the win. Hands and the aside cards are hidden; card counts, penalties, deals won, last actions and the pile are public. There is no talk.
